RENEWABLE JOINING: LOCAL COUNTERS, THERMAL LOAD PATHS AND MATERIAL RESET
13 November 2026 Brisbane / 12 November UTC

Scope and available construction
The available completed switchable-interface return describes a prepared 50 x 50 mm copper-seam joint, two 8 mm steel carriers, 100 spring-supported 2 x 2 mm islands, finite island moments and flow-accessible ribs. It is an introduced design, not a physical joint. Its return and visible activity retain their native identity, rendering, nested activity and uncollected report/archive limitations. No linked artifact or producer code was recovered or executed.

The return's available mechanics replace free scalar springs with four folded links per island and coupled carrier bending. Introduced pair stiffnesses are kn=1.061 MN/m, kx=ky=2.046 MN/m, and rotational stiffnesses 1.603/3.816/4.997 Nm/rad. The required tensile/shear interaction law uses 40/30 MPa with an introduced local concentration factor. The 8 mm carrier interaction is .799, with one corner absent .811 and ten edge islands absent .878. The last case times 1.15 proof is 1.0097; it cannot be treated as accepted under that same model. Source manufacturing, actual strength, fillets, seed adhesion, residual stress, fracture and creep are not thereby qualified.

Other available return contracts remain distinct: 5.225 mg useful Cu,15.868 C useful charge, .576 A peak and 22.6 s calculated growth to 50 nm separation plus 7.5 s additional charge. Near-touching and continuity do not construct a sound seam. Its 99.1/94.6/55 s phase allocations, 37.6 s stripping and 4% rejection are introduced; changing dissolved-Cu headroom from500 to100 mol/m3 gives about198 s complete release. The bath uses finite10 mL inventory and a paid counterfoil, with 631.33 mg functional copper. No renewal of its critical mask, seed, springs or seals was demonstrated.

Ionic geometry: a conditional improvement
